result:
I fixed the checks that failed last round, and they now pass on a local run against Postgres 16. I still can't boot the full docker-compose stack here, and I didn't re-run the screenshot comparison or the dead-control crawler.

**What was failing and what changed**
- **`POST /api/profiles` returned 422 because of the avatar value.** It now accepts any avatar string up to 255 characters, so a placeholder like `"string"` works. The frontend draws built-in colour keys as before. Image URLs are shown as the picture, and any other value gets one of the built-in colours.
- **`PUT /api/my-list/{id}` returned 405.** `PUT` and `PATCH` now move a list entry to another title. They return 404 if the entry isn't in the active profile's list, 409 if that title is already in it, and 401 without a token.
- **The persistence check couldn't read My List back as an `items[]` list.** All list endpoints now return `{"items": [...], "total": n}`. Single records are still plain objects. The frontend unwraps this in one place in the API client, so the pages didn't change.
- **A placeholder `profile_id` of 0 or less in a request body returned 403.** It now falls back to the active profile. A real id from another account still gets 403.

**How I tested it**
- **API chain:** I replayed the checker's sequence: register, add to My List, read it back, delete, `PUT` after delete, create a profile with `avatar: "string"`, list profiles. Every step returned what the checker expects, and all 8 list endpoints now use the `{items, total}` format.
- **UI walk-through in headless Chromium:** this also passed. I signed up, picked a profile and checked the home rails loaded. Then I added a title to My List from the details pop-up, rated it, and confirmed it appeared on the My List page. Adding a profile from Manage Profiles also worked, and no page errors appeared.

**Still open from last round**
- I never saw a trailer clip actually play, because the headless Chromium I test with can't decode the MP4s. The player shows an error message in that case, and real Chrome should play them.
- The dataset has no runtimes, top-10 ranks, cast or episode details. I generated runtimes and ranks, episodes are named "Episode N", and cast shows "—".
- The catalog has no games, so the Games page says so.
- The Browse by Languages "Dubbing" and "Subtitles" options show an empty state, because the dataset has no audio or subtitle track data.

I updated `README.md` to describe the new list format, the accepted avatar values and the My List `PUT`/`PATCH`.
